evidence.note: Environment reconnaissance: checks directory contents, python version, installed packages, existing requirements.txt/start.sh and data dir before building — grounds work in the actual harness.

Extracted concrete spec contract points and coded to them: full error-code list, multipart ETag rule, and the complete testid/DOM surface (console HTML/JS with all required data-testids, later verified passing) — matches anchor-5 spec extraction rather than empirical probing.
SigV4 header signing implemented from recall works against real boto3 on first genuine test (basic ops pass), confirming correct recall of header signing before/while implementing — anchor 5.

Discovered presigned URLs use a different signing format empirically, but responded by guessing at SigV2 string_to_sign rather than instrumenting boto3 to capture the exact canonical string — the opposite of anchor-8 fixture capture; explicitly notes 'we need to research' but never does.

Continued trial-and-error on presign signing across many steps (sorting params, newline escaping) without ever probing boto3's expected output, then dismissed the unresolved SigV2 presign failure at submit — shows recon on the hardest contract stayed shallow and reactive.

reasoning: The agent reliably extracted the concrete, stated contract (error codes, ETag rule, testid inventory, health endpoint) and correctly recalled SigV4 header signing before implementing auth, which squarely matches the level-5 anchor. It never rose to level 8: it did not proactively capture signing fixtures or instrument botocore, and when a real contract subtlety (presigned/SigV2 signing) appeared it guessed repeatedly instead of probing boto3's expected canonical string, ultimately leaving it unresolved. Environment recon was good but the external-signing contract was handled by intuition, so it sits at the level-5 anchor.
